name: Kevin Peterson
profile: Robotics engineer who co-founded sidewalk-delivery-robot company Marble (acquired by Caterpillar in 2020), then led perception for Waymo's autonomous trucking division. In 2024 he co-founded Bedrock Robotics with Boris Sofman and others; as CTO he leads its autonomous excavator system, now valued at 4.1B USD after a 600M USD Series C (Oct 2026).
interesting_fact: In July 2026 a Bedrock-equipped Caterpillar 352 excavator dug to grade and loaded a dump truck for hours with no one in the cab and no remote intervention; by Aug 2026 driverless excavators were working on three commercial sites in Texas and Nevada.
deep_cut_fact: His earlier startup Marble was acquired by Caterpillar in 2020 - and Bedrock's autonomy kit now runs on Caterpillar excavators such as the Cat 352.
notes: Lower profile than CEO Sofman; route via Bedrock press. A Kevin Peterson completed a CMU Robotics MS (2009, advisor Red Whittaker) but it is unconfirmed this is the same person. Data-center construction is a Bedrock target market (e.g. Haydon partnership).

name: Brian Barritt
profile: Network engineer behind the temporospatial software-defined networking (TS-SDN) that orchestrated Google's Loon balloon internet network; he co-founded Aalyria, the Google spinout commercialising that software ('Spacetime') for satellite, aerospace, 5G-NTN and defence networks. Aalyria is valued around 1B USD.
interesting_fact: Spacetime ran Loon's stratospheric mesh network in production for three years, serving hundreds of thousands of users across multiple continents, over E-band links highly vulnerable to rain and weather.
deep_cut_fact: Inside Google the software was codenamed 'Minkowski' (after the spacetime mathematician); Barritt co-authored with Wesley Eddy the 2016 AIAA paper 'SDN Enhancements for LEO Satellite Networks', which Aalyria still cites as a foundation of Spacetime.
notes: CTO title from theorg.com (another CTO also listed there, so title may have changed). Technical, publication-oriented; good for an episode on space/aerospace networking.

name: Willem Delbare
current_role: Co-Founder, CTO & CEO, Aikido Security (Ghent, Belgium / San Francisco)
profile: Belgian serial founder (including CRM company Teamleader) who co-founded Aikido Security in Oct 2022 with Roeland Delrue, Felix Garriau and Madeline Lawrence, after finding security tools made life as a CTO harder. Aikido's developer-first application security platform hit a 1B USD valuation with a 60M USD Series B in Jan 2026; it also launched the open-source Opengrep fork.
interesting_fact: His pitch: 'There have been security tools for three decades, but I think we're the first where the buyer is the user' - calling Aikido the 'no BS' security platform for developers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aikido he was a VC fund scout and frequent angel co-investor alongside his future co-founder Madeline Lawrence, who says they had known each other for years.
notes: Teamleader founding credit sourced to ITdaily (https://itdaily.com/blogs/security/aikido-security-without-nonsense/). Angel investor list from tech.eu Jan 2023. Aikido has offices in Ghent, SF, Chicago, London, Singapore.
